## Why This Benchmark Is Included

Recommendation accounts for a major sparse-ML systems workload class.

| **Field** | **Value** |
|:---|:---|
| **Classroom value** | Contrasts embedding tables with dense networks, and trains from scratch inside a class period. |
| **Systems behavior** | Embedding lookup, dense interaction, and negative-sampling data pressure. |
| **Benchmark lineage** | Direct inheritance from the MLPerf Training v0.5 recommendation workload, on the same historical-MLPerf basis that retains MiniGo as the reinforcement-learning identity. |
| **Model choice** | MLPerf Training v0.5 fixes the NCF architecture and its predictive-factor and MLP configuration. |
| **Dataset choice** | MovieLens-20M is the official v0.5 dataset and is roughly 190 MB, so the unchanged contract fits the declared laptop envelope. |
| **Quality metric** | MLPerf Training v0.5 publishes 0.635 HR@10 for this model, dataset, and evaluator. |
| **Published baseline** | MLPerf Training v0.5 recommendation quality target |
| **Alternative rejected** | DLRM on Criteo Terabyte preserves a richer sparse-memory profile but cannot execute in the declared envelope. DLRM on Criteo Kaggle would fit, but no published AUC target exists for that pairing, so adopting it would require inventing a threshold. |

## How to Run

```bash
# one-time asset preparation
uv run mlperf fetch --workload recommendation --profile max

# benchmark run (writes JSON/HTML/CSV reports + .provd.json provenance)
uv run mlperf run --workload recommendation --profile max

# quick smoke pass
uv run mlperf run --workload recommendation --profile min

# research envelope
uv run mlperf run --workload recommendation --profile pro
```

See the [running guide](../../guide/running.qmd) for profile semantics, report handling, and power measurement flags.

## Candidate Quality Target

| **Field** | **Value** |
|:---|:---|
| **Metric** | hit_rate_at_10 |
| **Target** | 0.635 |
| **Direction** | higher |
| **Target kind** | inherited acceptance gate |
| **Target basis** | literature |
| **Tolerance** | 0.0 |
| **Reference runs** | 0 |

**Reviewer notes:**

- The target is the MLPerf Training v0.5 recommendation quality target of 0.635 HR@10 for Neural Collaborative Filtering on MovieLens-20M. It is inherited, not project-created.
- MLPerf retired the NCF recommendation benchmark after v0.5 because MovieLens-20M was too small to differentiate datacenter-scale systems. That property is what makes it appropriate here, and it is the same historical-MLPerf basis on which MiniGo is retained as the reinforcement-learning identity.
- This replaces the DLRM and Criteo Terabyte contract, which could not execute inside the declared laptop envelope. That contract required manually licensed 1 TB data, a roughly 90 GB checkpoint, and a 256 GB-class runtime.
- The substitution changes what the workload teaches. NCF exercises embedding lookup and dense interaction, but its categorical cardinality is far below Criteo's, so it does not expose the memory-capacity wall that motivated DLRM. Record that limitation rather than implying equivalence.
- The parameter count is dominated by the user and item embedding tables and is left unverified until the runner constructs the model and reports it. Do not publish an estimated count.
- {'HR@10 is evaluated leave-one-out against 999 sampled negatives per user, for 1000 candidates per user. The count is part of the metric, not a tuning knob': 're-scoring one trained checkpoint at 100 negatives gives 0.9336 and at 999 gives 0.5474, so a smaller candidate set makes the published target trivially beatable. An initial draft of this contract used 100, the convention from the original NCF paper on smaller datasets, and produced an implausible first-epoch pass. A held-out-item leakage check over 500 sampled users found 0 contaminated users, confirming the split itself is sound and the candidate count was the sole cause.'}

## Systems Experiment Execution Contract

**Within-run measurement protocol:**

| **Field** | **Value** |
|:---|:---|
| **Primary metric** | train_and_eval_seconds |
| **Scenario** | training |
| **Timing scope** | MLPerf v0.5 NCF training loop through the epoch that reaches the target, including per-epoch HR@10 evaluation |
| **Included phases** | user and item index construction and device transfer, forward and backward passes, Adam optimizer steps, per-epoch leave-one-out HR@10 evaluation |
| **Excluded phases** | dataset fetching and CSV parsing, leave-one-out split construction and negative-sample generation, model construction, best-checkpoint serialization, final report and provenance serialization |
| **Device synchronization** | synchronize immediately before and after the measured training-and-evaluation region |
| **Outer reference runs** | 1 |
| **Outer preconditioning runs** | 0 |
| **Outer inter execution cooldown seconds** | 30 |
| **Repeatability metric** | train_and_eval_seconds |
| **Repeatability limit** | 0.05 |

## Results

Run the benchmark and read your own report:

```bash
uv run mlperf run --workload recommendation --profile max
```

Every run writes an HTML dashboard for reading, JSON for machine use, CSV for spreadsheets, and a `.provd.json` provenance manifest. Those artifacts carry the quality decision, timing distribution, hardware and software fingerprint, asset digests, and model lineage for the run you performed.

See [Reading Results](../../guide/results.qmd) for how to interpret them.
